metadata.summary: Roger Federer is set to make a long-anticipated return to play at Flushing Meadows as the five-time consecutive US Open men's singles champion will play in an exhibition match, live on Sky Sports.
metadata.content: Roger Federer returns to play US Open exhibition match, live on Sky Sports - but has no interest in professional comeback | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content Roger Federer returns to play US Open exhibition match, live on Sky Sports - but has no interest in professional comeback Roger Federer will return to play at Flushing Meadows for the first time since 2019, as the five-time US Open champion features in an exhibition event; watch Roger Federer: An Icon Returns to New York live on Sky Sports Main Event on Wednesday morning at 1am BST Monday 24 August 2026 22:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roger Federer said he was nervous about returning to the court after having not played a Grand Slam match since 2021 Roger Federer is set to make a long-anticipated return to play at Flushing Meadows as the five-time consecutive US Open men's singles champion will play in an exhibition match, live on Sky Sports . The 45-year-old will walk out onto the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium as a player for the first time since he was beaten by Grigor Dimitrov in 2019. After a knee injury prevented him from entering the draw for the 2020 US Open, Federer would not return to play at the Grand Slam before announcing his retirement in September 2022. metadata.summary: Cole Palmer looked like Cole Palmer again but Chelsea's progress this season will be hampered by sticking with Robert Sanchez in goal, argued Jamie Carragher.
metadata.content: Cole Palmer's back, an electric Chelsea attack - but goalkeeper problem remains after opening Premier League win at Fulham | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Cole Palmer's back, an electric Chelsea attack - but goalkeeper problem remains after opening Premier League win at Fulham Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers all score to give Chelsea 3-2 victory at Fulham; Palmer was outstanding but Robert Sanchez came in for criticism from Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher, who said it's "impossible" for Chelsea to win the title with Sanchez in goal Monday 24 August 2026 23:49, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Monday Night Football panel discuss Cole Palmer's brilliant display for Chelsea as they won 3-2 away to west London rivals Fulham. Cole Palmer looked like Cole Palmer again but Chelsea's progress this season will be hampered by sticking with Robert Sanchez in goal, argued Jamie Carragher. Palmer was back to his best in the 3-2 win over Fulham , producing the kind of performance that reminded everyone why he has become one of the Premier League's most explosive players. There was swagger to his performance again - the confidence, invention and end product that made him such a phenomenon when he first arrived at Stamford Bridge. Speaking to Sky Sports , Palmer, when asked if he was ready to go this season, replied: "Did you not watch the game? I'm only joking, I'm ready. It was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot
